purpose: Discriminate Clay-repository workflow/label failure from a broader execution-transport availability problem without creating another runtime dispatch.

interpretation.observed: The current ChatGPT execution container cannot enter the documented SSH bridge directly, and an independent controller-repository self-hosted probe was still queued at observation time.
interpretation.inferred: Evidence weakens the narrow hypothesis that Clay-repository labels/workflow syntax alone cause the queue and is more compatible with a repo-spanning self-hosted scheduling/transport availability problem.

counterhypotheses: The ChatGPT network namespace may reject these SSH routes even while the owner bridge works from another machine.
The self-hosted runner may be online but unable to accept jobs because of GitHub-side registration, runner-group, concurrency, service-account, or scheduling state.
The VPS/container may be healthy while only the ingress/runner transport is unavailable.
next_high_information_gate: Restore or expose one already-authorized transport into clay-direct-dev and obtain one terminal CLAY_DIRECT_DEV_ROUNDTRIP/v1 result; do not create another generation-0 dispatch merely because another go was received.
